description: Within Earth's magnetic field, energetic particles are trapped in two doughnut-shaped regions known as the Van Allen radiation belts—usually separated by a gap where particles are especially sparse. This structure can be dramatically rearranged during solar storms, but until now, astronomers have remained largely unsure as to how this happens.
title: Four radiation belts surrounded Earth for weeks after 2024 solar superstorm

description: They are single-celled, tiny and vital to life on Earth. Phytoplankton, which drift freely in the water column, provide food and oxygen for other marine organisms, while consuming CO₂ and nutrients—much like plants on land.
title: Offshore wind turbine hum may make phytoplankton grow faster

description: Climate change is affecting the environmental conditions of wildlife around the world: Rising temperatures, changing precipitation patterns and more frequent extreme weather events can lead to important food sources becoming unavailable, at least temporarily. How well animals cope with such changes also depends on how flexibly they can adapt their behavior to new conditions.
title: Guinea baboons respond flexibly to changing environmental conditions

description: Cornell researchers have found a novel way to boost immunity against cancer: using ancient virus-derived machinery to produce tiny extracellular vesicles that carry antigen information across long distances to rally immune cells.
title: Ancient cellular machinery boosts immunity against cancer

description: Socioeconomic differences in health may be greater than research suggests. In a new thesis, Balram Rai used PSA testing in the Stockholm region as an example and investigated how socioeconomic position can be measured at different levels and how measurement errors can affect inferences about inequalities in health.
title: Q&A: How socioeconomic status is measured can obscure inequalities in health care

description: QUT researchers have developed a modeling framework to quantify microplastic inputs from urban surfaces to ecologically sensitive water environments such as Moreton Bay.
title: Roads store microplastics before they join rain runoff to waterways

description: A decade-long project in remote northwestern Australia suggests archaeologists should rethink a long-held assumption about the diets of humans almost 50,000 years ago.
title: Diverse diets may reflect choice, not scarcity, among Australian hunters 45,000 years ago

description: Engineers have long known that diamond could transform modern electronics because of its exceptional hardness and superior thermal conductivity, but building with it remains challenging.
title: Engineers develop simpler, scalable way to make diamond nanowires

description: Gratitude lists can help anyone recognize the good things in their lives and feel more positive. But do they inspire people to give back? Research by BYU psychology professor Jenae Nelson suggests that becoming a grateful person takes more than counting blessings.
title: Study explores how gratitude can become a character trait

description: It's been nearly a year since Australia's under-16 social media ban came into effect. The restrictions were touted as a measure to protect young people from harmful design features that keep them online longer, while shielding them from risks that come with using social media.
title: Six ways teens can better protect themselves from online harms

description: The tiny Irukandji jellyfish Carukia barnesi lives in the waters of northern Australia, predominantly in Queensland, with similar species in Western Australia. Irukandji stings can be lethal. These stings can cause a range of symptoms—nausea, muscle pain, vomiting and traumatic psychological effects.
title: Warmer water reshapes venom chemistry in tiny jellyfish

description: By targeting the biological processes that determine fungal virulence, microbiologists from Stellenbosch University are suggesting a promising new strategy for combating emerging fungal infections.
title: Outsmarting deadly fungi: Researchers identify promising strategy against emerging fungal infections

description: Besides fires and floods, droughts and storms, another type of extreme weather may be getting more common due to climate change: lightning. Globally, in a future of high greenhouse gas emissions, lightning may get 76% to 140% more common by the end of the century than between 1995 and 2014, according to a new study published in Earth's Future.
title: Lightning could strike more than twice as often in a warming world

description: One of Australia's largest and longest studies of bull shark habits has identified their preferred conditions for nearshore swimming—and warmer waters in summer and autumn are top of the list.
title: Bull shark records reveal links between warmer waters, rainfall and activity near Queensland beaches

description: Over $1 billion a year. That is what a small parasitic weed plant costs maize farmers across sub-Saharan Africa every year, without ever being caught in the act. Striga, known as witchweed, latches onto maize roots underground and siphons off water and nutrients long before it breaks the surface. By the time a farmer sees the damage, the blame falls on drought or exhausted soil. For 30 years nobody could put a reliable figure on the bill, and without one, the response stayed scattered.
title: Witchweed menaces maize farms across Africa: New study maps the damage

description: Indigenous fire management in Australia provides one of the world's best examples of how traditional methods can protect fire-prone environments, and this inclusive approach should be prioritized in modern conservation, according to research led by Charles Darwin University (CDU).
title: Indigenous land management practices can deliver improved conservation outcomes, study notes

description: While right-leaning governments around the world are railing against workforce diversity, equity and inclusion (DEI) measures that have been in place for over two decades, researchers note that the diversity of staff within hospitality and tourism businesses around the world—and the diverse customers they serve—requires a strong DEI framework to best serve these industries.
title: Strategies to ensure DEI workforce safeguards in hospitality and tourism

description: Strawberry powdery mildew (PM), caused by the fungus Podosphaera fragariae, is a serious disease that can affect leaves, flowers, fruit and other aerial parts of strawberry plants. Infection can reduce both crop yields and fruit quality. The disease often first appears as white patches on the underside of leaves before spreading to the upper surface, making early detection challenging.
title: Beneficial fungus could offer a new way to control strawberry powdery mildew

description: Much of the bycatch in tropical fisheries is kept as "trash fish," which is processed into fishmeal, mainly for aquaculture feed. But this bycatch contains many juvenile fish, and there is concern that catching so many juveniles could lead to a decrease in the adult population. A new study led by researchers at Thailand's Department of Fisheries and Hokkaido University suggests that in these fisheries, the loss of juveniles might be partly offset by better survival among the remaining juveniles.
title: Nature may cushion the impact of catching juvenile fish in tropical fisheries

description: A caring and supportive manager sounds like a dream for any employee, but could too much kindness turn "perfect" staff members into exhausted workaholics?
title: Perfect employees and managers may not be the perfect match

description: Particles can generally move between neighboring sites in a crystal, a solid in which atoms are arranged in a regular, repeating pattern, or an optical lattice, an arrangement of laser-based traps that confines atoms. A strong potential gradient (i.e., a steep change in potential energy across a crystal or lattice) makes this ordinary particle hopping difficult and energetically costly.
title: Ultracold atoms reveal first direct view of bound-pair motion in a fracton system

description: Exceptionally high tides and El Niño-fueled weather were threatening the California coast with possibly extreme flooding during the busiest U.S. travel week of the year.
title: California braces for triple flooding threat of huge tides, El Niño, warm oceans

description: China on Tuesday unveiled the crew for its Shenzhou 24 spacecraft ahead of this week's launch, with a Pakistani set to become the first foreign astronaut to board its space station.
title: China unveils new space mission crew, with a Pakistani astronaut set to board its space station

description: A team of astronomers led by Julien Wolf, a postdoctoral researcher at the Max Planck Institute for Astronomy (MPIA) in Heidelberg, Germany (now at the European Southern Observatory in Garching bei München, Germany), discovered the most distant quasar to date. First identified in the Euclid Wide Survey (EWS), the object was confirmed to be a quasar by subsequent observations with some of the most powerful telescopes on the ground and in space.
title: New quasar record tightens constraints on black hole formation scenarios
